reports.title: NEWS CORPORATION REPORTS FIRST QUARTER RESULTS FOR FISCAL 2027

desk.headline: Revenue up 6% to $2.28bn and adjusted EPS of $0.28 beat estimates; profit up sharply; no formal outlook given
results: Sales rose 6% to $2.28bn (4% excluding currency and deals); Total Segment EBITDA rose 19% to $403m and net income 43% to $215m.
Dow Jones sales grew 8% to $630m, with Risk & Compliance up 11% and Energy up 8%; digital-only news subscriptions rose 10% to nearly 6.5m.
Digital real estate profit jumped 34% to $212m; REA sales rose 13% to $369m (8 points from a stronger Aussie dollar), while Realtor.com sales grew 5% but users fell 8% and leads 11%.
Book publishing sales rose 9% to $582m; News Media sales slipped 1% and its EBITDA fell 40% to $18m.
Free cash flow was -$89m (from +$4m) on working-capital timing and higher tax; $166m went on buybacks and $61m on dividends.

guidance.summary: News Corp gives no numeric outlook in the release. On the call, as reported, management made no change to its outlook and gave only segment-by-segment trend comments.

points: CEO Robert Thomson stressed paid content deals with tech platforms and legal action against unpaid use: "we will woo and we will sue."
Management reaffirmed its target of $1bn in Dow Jones EBITDA by fiscal 2030, as reported.
Housing is softer: Australian October listings fell 13% (8% adjusting for working days), and higher US mortgage rates weigh on Realtor.com.
Free cash flow is expected to be weighted to the second half, with management confident of a strong full year.
News Media is expected to trend like Q1 with some extra California Post costs; REA agreed to buy a 35% stake in Distilled (Daft.ie) for about US$290m.
call.source: Call coverage: Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 4 Nov 2026; Quartr call summary, 5 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Australian and US housing listings, which drive REA and Realtor.com.
Whether free cash flow recovers in the second half as promised.
New content-licensing deals or lawsuits with tech platforms.
